Counting from the original position gives the same answer, because the head fell 4 metres and the interface rose 4 times 40, or 160 metres, from 320. questions.explanation: A water account keeps two kinds of term apart, and the difference is whether a number can be added to or taken from a store. A lake has a volume, so its level can stay put over a dry week while the same water passes through it, and a storm makes its level rise by an amount that then appears in the storage term. A stream has no volume to subtract from, only a measured discharge, so it can only ever contribute to the flux side of the balance. This is why a reservoir is sometimes called a source and a river a sink in the same account, and why an account that lists a lake among its fluxes has confused the two.

questions.explanation: Infiltration capacity is a property of the surface, and it is limited by whatever the water has to pass through to get into the profile. A crust of fine particles plugs the small pores at the very top, so entry slows even though the bulk of the soil beneath is unchanged, and deep tillage breaks the crust and reopens connected macropores that let water in faster than the small pores alone would allow. The case for total porosity fails because tillage barely changes the volume of pore space while changing its continuity, and a pore that is present but disconnected does not transmit water. This is also why a surface that has been driven over repeatedly, and a soil that has been puddled, differ in intake even when their analyses are identical.

questions.explanation: Saline intrusion is a response to a head difference, and the interface moves because pumping has lowered the freshwater head, so the only measures that reverse it are ones that raise that head again. questions.explanation: In most fresh water the limiting nutrient is phosphorus, so the size of the population the lake can carry is set by how much phosphorus arrives. Add phosphorus and the limit rises, which means the biomass the system can support rises with it, and the visible result is a larger standing crop of algae rather than a faster version of the old one. That is why a small percentage reduction in a load can look like no change at all while the system is still far above its original limit, and why the interesting number is the concentration the load produces rather than the change in it. A shading or burial effect would change what a given nutrient supply supports, not how much supply the system has.

questions.explanation: Three independent terms meet in that reach, and the lowest reading comes from all three pointing the wrong way at once. Warm water holds less dissolved oxygen at saturation, so the ceiling falls; decomposing plant material raises the biological and chemical demand, so the oxygen is consumed; and slow flow lowers the rate at which the surface reaerates the water, so it is replaced slowly. questions.explanation: Thirty years of accumulation has put phosphorus into the sediments, and the sediments are inside the system that is supposed to have been cleaned up. questions.explanation: A ground-level concentration is a mass of pollutant divided by a volume of air, and the report's mixing height is what tells you the volume being used. The same emission spread through 250 m gives a higher concentration than the same emission spread through 1,000 m, which is why a still, shallow winter afternoon can produce the worst reading of the year at a site whose annual emissions are modest. questions.explanation: A temperature inversion is warm air sitting above cold air, and that arrangement is stable, because a parcel displaced upward finds denser air above it and sinks back, and one displaced downward finds lighter air and rises back. With no vertical motion, a release has no way to leave the surface layer, so it accumulates until sunrise breaks the inversion and mixes the column out. A valley makes this worse on clear windless nights, because the cold air drains down the slopes and pools on the floor, and the effect can be strong enough to shift a whole day's maximum. The pollutant's own weight is irrelevant at these concentrations, and the ordering in the second option is the single most common way the mechanism gets remembered backwards.

A soil with a high acid-neutralising capacity takes up hydrogen ions while releasing base cations, so the water passing through it stays near neutral and the lake receives water that is not yet acid. A soil with little capacity has nothing to give, so the input passes through and the lake's pH falls. This is why the deposition record alone cannot predict damage, and why a survey of soils is a precondition of any assessment. It is also why the recovery of a damaged catchment is slow, because the base that was leached out during the acidifying years is no longer there to be returned.

questions.explanation: A reservoir account has three terms, the inflow, the release and the change in what is stored, and the third is exactly the one that decides the claim. answer.ex: A good design needs a period of pumping at a measured and reported rate, a recovery period afterwards, and a control well that is never pumped, with water levels in both logged continuously. answer.ex: An unconfined aquifer gains recharge directly beneath the surface where the rain falls, so its water table responds at once and the response is spread over the area that received the rain. A confined aquifer gains recharge only where the water table of the aquifer above it is in hydraulic contact with it, which is normally a fraction of its own area and may be far away, so a confined aquifer can rise in one place while continuing to fall under pumping in another. The consequence for a programme is that a confined aquifer cannot be managed from the well alone, since the pumping point and the recharge point are in different places with different land use, and a catchment-scale change to the surface is the only thing that adds water to it. answer.ex: The nutrient is not only in the water but in the sediments, and a lake that has been fertilised for decades has built a store there. When the water goes hypoxic the sediments change behaviour: instead of holding on to phosphorus they release some of it back into the overlying water, and the released phosphorus fertilises the algae, which die and sink, which consumes more oxygen and produces more release. The external reduction and this internal release therefore work against each other, and a lake can sit at a substantially higher level than the new input alone would support, often for a decade or more. Recovery, when it comes, is also not a reversal, because the base that was leached out during the acidifying and oxygen-poor years has to be replaced, the species composition has usually changed, and the nutrients already fixed into the food web have to be worked through. A management plan that treats a large cut in input as sufficient is therefore likely to be disappointed.

answer.ex: Hardness counts two ions, calcium and magnesium, and it is reported as though all of it were calcium carbonate so that one number covers both. Neither ion has a taste at drinking concentrations, neither is a contaminant, and both are required in the diet, so a hard water is a nuisance rather than a hazard, with scale in kettles and soap that will not lather. Every risk that does matter is outside the number. Microbial safety is a matter of organisms and is addressed by disinfection, heavy metals such as lead, copper and arsenic are separate ions that a hardness test does not see, and dissolved salts, nitrate and fluoride each need their own analysis. A hardness figure is therefore genuinely useful for predicting what a water will do to pipes and kettles, and useless as a statement about whether the water is safe, which is the confusion the two very different uses invite.

answer.ex: Evaporation from a reservoir surface moves the same water from one place to another, so what it is depends entirely on where the boundary of the account is drawn. In a water account for the reservoir and the river that feeds it, the reservoir is inside the boundary and the water that leaves it by evaporation is a loss, and it is a real loss because it is no longer available to the users downstream. In an account for the whole river basin, the same water is still inside the boundary, having moved from the reservoir to the atmosphere, so it does not appear as a loss and only the water that finally leaves the basin is deducted. A figure of water available for use has to declare which of the two it is counting, and the choice changes the answer substantially in a hot dry year, because it is precisely in such a year that evaporation is large. The two accounts are both correct, which is why a water budget that mixes a reservoir loss into a basin balance can double-count or hide the same cubic metre.

questions.explanation: The sequence starts with the primary emissions, because until nitrogen dioxide is in the air there is nothing for the sunlight to act on. Photolysis then splits the molecule and the free oxygen atom joins molecular oxygen to make ozone, which is the step that makes the product without any stack having emitted it. The ozone converts nitrogen monoxide back to nitrogen dioxide and gives back molecular oxygen, which is the reaction that recycles the nitrogen oxides and holds the system in its daytime cycle, and it is also why the two nitrogen oxides rise together in a plume. The volatile organic compounds come last because they are the second reactant, reacting with the oxidant to make peroxy radicals and secondary products such as nitrates, and it is their presence that is what turns a cycle of nitrogen oxides into a photochemical episode.
questions.hint: No oxidant exists before the primary emissions arrive, and the secondary product needs a precursor.
questions.learningObjective: order the steps that build a secondary oxidant in sunlight

options.text: Nitrogen dioxide is split by sunlight, releasing an oxygen atom that joins molecular oxygen to form ozone
Nitrogen dioxide is released from traffic and from fuel combustion during the morning
Volatile organic compounds react with the oxidant, forming a peroxy radical and a nitrate
Ozone reacts with nitrogen monoxide, regenerating nitrogen dioxide and molecular oxygen

questions.explanation: The lime has to dissolve first, because the carbonate brings hydrogen ions down and raises the pH of the soil solution, and until it has, the exchange sites have no reason to change what they hold. The higher pH then shifts the balance on the exchange complex, so hydrogen ions come off the sites into solution and calcium occupies the vacated charge, which is the step that actually reduces acidity. Calcium and magnesium now in excess are free to be leached below the rooting zone, so the process also exports base from the profile, which is why liming raises the pH more than the added calcium alone would suggest. The measured exchangeable acidity falls and the bicarbonate concentration rises, and both of those are the observable consequences rather than steps in the chain, so they belong at the end.
questions.hint: Nothing can be displaced before the solution's chemistry has changed, and the measurement follows both.
questions.learningObjective: order the steps of a soil's response to liming

options.text: The lime dissolves and the pH of the soil solution rises
Base cations released from the exchange sites are carried away below the root zone
Hydrogen ions held on the exchange sites are displaced and calcium takes their place
The measured exchangeable acidity falls and the bicarbonate concentration in the soil rises

questions.explanation: Everything begins with the head, because the interface responds to the pressure difference above it and not to the pumping directly. As the cone of depression deepens, the potentiometric head falls, and the hydrostatic balance that held the fresh water over the salt water means a falling head is a rising interface. That interface then rises towards the well's screen, and the moment it passes the screen's depth the well begins to draw the denser saline water underneath. Only after that does the chloride in the discharge rise, which is why the chemistry is a lagging indicator and a poor trigger for action, by which time the head loss and the interface rise are already established and the well's own water is being lost. An early warning has to come from the head and from interface-tracking wells instead.
questions.hint: The head has to move before the interface can, and the interface before the screen is reached.
questions.learningObjective: order the events that connect coastal pumping to saline intrusion

options.text: Pumping lowers the piezometric head that stands above the fresh-salt interface
The hydrostatic balance then lifts the interface, because the head above it has fallen
The rising interface passes the depth at which the well's screen is set
Saline water is drawn into the well and the chloride in its discharge rises

questions.explanation: Wind erosion is a sequence that begins with a condition rather than an event, because the shear stress at the soil surface has to exceed a threshold set by the size, the coherence and the arrangement of the grains before any of them move. The first grains to respond are the largest, which roll and hop along the surface without leaving it, and this creep stage is also what knocks finer particles loose and abrades the clods. Once the stress is high enough, grains are lifted clear and travel in a bouncing cloud of short flights, which is saltation and the stage that does most of the transporting. The finest particles are the last and the most easily moved, becoming suspended in the airflow and carried well beyond the field, which is why the sediment found far downwind is fine even though the soil that supplied it was not.
questions.hint: Nothing moves before the stress at the surface reaches the threshold for the grains that are there.
questions.learningObjective: order the processes of wind erosion by grain size

options.text: The shear stress at the surface rises above the threshold set by the grains present
The largest grains start to roll and hop along the surface without leaving it
Grains are lifted clear and move in a bouncing cloud of short flights
The finest particles are entrained into the airflow and carried off the field
